vetoLines: Mr. Don Slesnick, Government Supervisors Association of Florida (GSAF), noted that the GSAF Board represented employees from every County department, and that these employees provided services to both incorporated and unincorporated areas of the county. He clarified that the supervisors in GSAF were first line supervisors who did hands on work with rank and file employees. He noted, for the record, that the Mayor’s veto caused this issue to come before the Commission at this meeting, and that GSAF had filed a grievance against the Mayor’s veto. Mr. Slesnick expressed concern with the Mayor vetoeing the Commission’s action to resolve the impasse, despite making an agreement with the union to have the County Commission resolve the impasse. He noted, for the record, that State Statutes designated the action by the Commission to resolve the impasse as the final decision and explained that 94 percent of GSAF members approved the Commission’s action based on the understanding that it was the final decision.

vetoLines: County Attorney Cuevas pointed out that the foregoing proposed resolution along with Agenda Items 2A3, 2A4, and 2A5 involved the Collective Bargaining Impasse resolutions, which were considered and adopted by this Commission on January 5, 2012 and subsequently vetoed by Mayor Gimenez on January 11, 2012. He advised members of the Commission that if they were to reconsider Collective Bargaining items or were unable to obtain the 2/3 vote required to override the Mayoral veto, the impasses for those four Unions would remain open. He noted these items were advertised for public hearing today (1/24) to allow the Commission to resolve the impasses.

County Attorney Robert Cuevas indicated that the PBA items were listed on today’s agenda as items 2A2 and 2A3, and that the agenda had a note in the margin explaining a public hearing for these items would be held if the County Commission reconsidered them or the Mayor’s veto was sustained. He stated the public hearings for agenda items 2A2 and 2A3 were publicly advertised in the “Miami Review.”

Mr. Rivera pointed out the County was going through the hiring process for corrections officers at the same time the Mayor was stating layoffs were possible. He noted the Mayor vetoing the Commission’s action that resolved the impasse on January 5, 2012, was improper under Chapter 447 of the State of Florida Statutes. He explained that the Mayor’s January 19 memorandum was only one-third correct. Mr. Rivera noted the County was planning to hire 100 fire fighters. He suggested the County reclassify the MDPD and Corrections and Rehabilitation Department employees who were going to be laid off as fire fighters. He stressed that this issue was one of integrity, and pointed out that the Mayor promised he would not lay off police officers.

Commissioner Suarez noted, for the record, the Commission started with a goal to save $430 million with employee concessions representing $239 million. He pointed out the Commission had accomplished this goal, except for $65 million. He explained that Chairman Martinez had proposed a 2.5 percent healthcare contribution by County employees, and that he supported that proposal; however, the Mayor had indicated he would veto such action. Commissioner Suarez expressed concern that the Mayor was a party in the declared impasse, yet he had the ability to veto actions made by the Commission in resolving that impasse.

matter.recommendation: It is recommended that the Board of County Commissioners (Board) approve the proposed settlement of the lawsuit. gaps: Window 1998-06-16 (Barreiro first seated; 6/16/1998 minutes accept the canvassing certificate for the June 2, 1998 District 5 special election) to 2020-11-16 (last BCC meeting before Gimenez left the mayor's office on 2020-11-17). 924 of the 926 listed meetings in the window read (BCC list CC, plus ZB 2017-07 on and CDMP 2017-04 on).
Not read: commminute.asp?cmbmeetdate=4342 (2019-10-30 CDMP meeting) and 1317 (second 2003-05-20 entry) return the county error page. See needs-browser.md.

BCC zoning hearings before 2017-07-20 are not in the Clerk's online minutes (the ZB and CDMP lists start 2017). Site-specific zoning votes 1998-06..2017-07 are therefore missing; RER results PDFs are listed in needs-browser.md.

Universe: final votes (Adopted, Approved, Approved with conditions/staff recommendation, Denied, motion failed) on resolutions, ordinances, zoning items, change orders and professional service agreements, including files later vetoed. First readings, deferrals, withdrawals, items amended into a new file (the new file is used) are left out; a file appears once, at its last final vote.

Excluded by rule: urging/opposing/supporting, codesignations and naming, appointments, proclamations and commendations, directives for reports or studies, millage, special taxing districts and assessment rolls, omnibus and district discretionary or reserve allocations, in-kind allocations, and code amendments (ORDINANCE RELATING TO ...) unless they grant something to a named party.

Parties are taken from the item title: corporate and organization names (Inc., LLC, Ltd., Corp., Company, L.P., P.A., JV, Association, Foundation, union locals, etc.), FILED BY on plats, and the applicant field on zoning items. Government entities are dropped. An item whose title names no private party is left out and listed in unnamed.json (with the reason). About 40 of 6,148 extracted names are title fragments, not clean names. Titles are English only.

In-kind service allocations (county park, transit or police services for an event run by a named group, charged to a district in-kind reserve) are excluded as district allocations, as in the county list; 1,277 of them are in unnamed.json.
"Bid Awards" (BID AWARD RECOMMENDATIONS) packages in 1998-2004 minutes name no vendor in the title; their vendors are only in the attached packets and are not in this list.

Rolls: every member present that day is yes unless the vote line lists No, Absent, Absent OCB (shown absent), Excused, or Absent COI (shown recused); late arrivals are absent for votes taken before they arrived when the printed tally requires it. Every printed tally matches the roll.

Lobbyists: Clerk historical registrations (www2.miamidadeclerk.gov/lobbyhist), searched by principal name; a registration counts when the principal name equals the party (ignoring punctuation, "&"/AND and corporate suffix) and the lobbyist was employed on or before the vote, in the vote year or the year before. annualRegistration says whether the lobbyist's own annual registration list covers the vote year (null = list not retrieved). The archive's annual lists have gaps for many lobbyists, so it is shown, not used as a filter. Firms are not in the archive.

Mayor fields (Gimenez, 2011-07-07..2020-11-16): memoFrom and recommendation are copied from the matter page's legislative text (the cover memorandum's From line and its RECOMMENDATION section); titleAuthorizesMayorToExecute / titleRatifiesMayorAction come from the item title; vetoed means the Clerk's file type for the item is "Mayoral Veto"; veto.overrideVotes are the override roll calls from the minutes. Contracts actually signed by the Mayor are not in the records read here.
